functions.plate_comment: Accepted C reconstruction: ResetVector. The C body expresses the terminal FirmwareMainLoop handoff; C251 5.60 O8 emits a single EJMP. Focused host test passes. The former same-address vector assembly entry was removed.

Accepted C reconstruction: ControllerEventInterruptEntry. C explicitly owns SFR:D1 bit-three publication/restoration and handler dispatch; C251 interrupt code preserves registers and emits RETI. Focused host test passes. Same-address assembly removed.

Accepted C reconstruction: HostInterfaceInterruptEntry. C dispatches the handler and converts the RAM:00fa alternate interrupt-return rewrite into an explicit RestartFirmware transfer after clearing the request. C251 interrupt listing and focused tests pass. Same-address assembly removed.

Accepted C reconstruction: ControllerPacketInterruptEntry. C explicitly owns SFR:D1 bit-four publication/restoration and handler dispatch; C251 interrupt code preserves registers and emits RETI. Focused host test passes. Same-address assembly removed.

Accepted C reconstruction: Timer0InterruptEntry. Interrupt-qualified C dispatches Timer0TickHandler; C251 emits register preservation and RETI. Focused host test passes. Same-address assembly removed.

Accepted C reconstruction: SfrE1Bit7InterruptEntry. C explicitly publishes interrupted PSW into SFR:D1 after the handler, preserving the canonical double-PUSH-PSW effect; C251 emits RETI. Focused host test passes. Same-address assembly removed.

Builds the 96-byte standard INQUIRY response at RAM:00dcc5. It writes the fixed response header, copies vendor, product, revision, and build-date bytes from RAM:f80000..f8002f, and zeros response offsets 0x38..0x5f.

When RAM:000c7f equals 0x81, fills InquiryResponseBuffer offsets 0x2e through 0x31 with spaces and copies six bytes from RAM:00dd25 through 00dd2a to response offsets 0x32 through 0x37. Otherwise leaves the response unchanged. This is used only by the vendor-EF response builder.
Copies ACC bytes from DR4 to DR0 after setting the internal index to zero and the exclusive limit to ACC. Only WR2 and WR6 advance, so both far pointers remain in their original 64-KiB banks.
Internal indexed byte-copy loop. Copies from DR4 to DR0 while unsigned R9 is below unsigned B, incrementing WR2, WR6, and R9 after each byte.
Returns the signed 16-bit absolute value of WR6 in WR6. The two's-complement minimum 0x8000 remains 0x8000.

Algorithm:
Computes the floating-point ceiling as negate, floor, negate.

Parameters:
Native floating-point register frame.

Returns:
Native ERET return carrying the transformed floating-point value.

Evidence:
Firmware 1.04 canonical bytes at RAM:f849f3..f849ff; direct wrapper review. Exact A251 boundary in src/platform/media_interrupt_leaves.a51.
Non-returning default coroutine-2 entry. Clears its transfer state, resets the raw-read queue, and yields coroutine 2 forever.

IEEE-754 binary64 floor.

Algorithm:
Clears all significand bits below the unbiased binary exponent. If the input is negative and any cleared bit was nonzero, subtracts one from the truncated value. Integral values, magnitudes at least 2^52, signed zero, and ordinary infinities and NaNs pass through. The firmware runtime's canonical all-ones NaN payload is an observed exception and returns -1.0.

Parameters:
DR0:DR4 / double value.

Returns:
DR0:DR4 / double floor result through ERET.

Reconstruction:
Accepted C implementation: src/platform/floating_floor.c. Complete firmware 1.04 review covers RAM:f84a14..RAM:f84adc. Focused IEEE vectors and Keil differential coverage include the all-ones runtime NaN; C251 5.60 FLOAT64 builds with zero diagnostics and ERET; obsolete same-address 201-byte A251 body/export removed.
Initializes read-runtime state by calling InitializeReadRuntimePointersAndFlags followed by InitializeReadRuntimeAddressC35.
Non-returning default coroutine-3 entry. Clears RAM:00fb9a and yields coroutine 3 forever.

Non-returning coroutine-1 drive-initialization entry selected by restart paths. Clears controller and shared acquisition state, runs InitializeDriveControlSequence, then restarts coroutine 1 at RunStartupSequenceCoroutine1 or RunStartupStatusCoroutine1 according to the result.
Coroutine 1 startup-sequence entry. Resets startup state, runs the initial drive sequence, then replaces coroutine 1 with the RAM:f852eb continuation before returning to the scheduler.

Algorithm: normalizes erased RAM:00fabd..00fabf calibration bytes into RAM:00fadd, RAM:00fade, and RAM:00fadf (also copies the first into RAM:00fadc); reads configuration offset 0x2c into RAM:00fac0; and derives RAM:00fc0f as 0xa0 for erased input or the byte plus 0xd8.

Parameters: none.

Returns: no scalar result; RET.

Accepted C reconstruction: src/startup/controller_calibration_configuration.c.

Firmware 1.04 RAM:f84d25..RAM:f84ed9 is a no-input ERET worker. It preserves the ordered RAM:00fad7/RAM:00faac/RAM:001304 policy for profile bytes 0, 1, 0x11, 0x12 and the default class; reads configuration tuples (0x20,RAM:00fab4,0x1a), (0x30,RAM:00fac4,4), and (0x3f,RAM:00fae0,1); applies the 0xff defaults; derives RAM:00fc14; writes E8/E9; scales unsigned RAM:00fabc by binary32 234/100 into RAM:000ffe; copies RAM:00fabd to RAM:00face; mirrors RAM:00fae0 bit two to BITS:0044; and conditionally sets bit six for indexed state four.

Focused host tests cover all selector classes, indexed results, erased/retained defaults, configuration tuples, float scaling and final bit state. Keil C251 5.60 optimization 0/8 emits the expected binary32 runtime calls/constants, direct BITS:0044 and ERET; drive and guard callers emit ECALL. Keil A251 4.69 rebuilds after removing the obsolete 437-byte body/export and now-unneeded address adapter.
Initializes the 32-bit read-runtime values at RAM:0015b3 and RAM:0015b7 to 0x00000fae and 0x0000faab, then clears their associated flags and counters.

Accepted C reconstruction: src/startup/drive_state_machine.c (behavior-tested). No explicit inputs or scalar result; native ERET coroutine-one entry. Preserves direct BITS:0039/P3 transitions, optional calibration reload, cooperative RAM:00faeb wait, complete disc-recognition result mapping, indexed-state service/configuration, media-type-two interpolation, mode-specific media-read initialization, and restart targets RAM:fa6e33/RAM:f85d74. Focused host tests pass; Keil C251 5.60 OPTIMIZE(0)/(8) emits the expected direct bits, helper call classes and ERET; reduced A251 unit passes after same-address assembly removal.

Accepted C reconstruction: src/startup/indexed_drive_state_transitions.c (behavior-tested). No explicit inputs or scalar result; native near RET and LCALL from RAM:f84f6a. Preserves all media/profile/calibration rejection predicates, reason codes 0x27/0x39/0x3a/0x3b/0x3d, ConfigurationWordFAAC bit-one clearing, fatal-signal gates, accepted write-speed replacement, state-five calibration persistence, and state-0x12 restart to RAM:f859f0. Focused host tests pass; Keil C251 5.60 OPTIMIZE(0)/(8) verifies near RET and caller LCALL; reduced A251 passes after same-address assembly removal.

Coroutine-1 continuation installed by the startup sequence and selected drive-retry paths. Clears acquisition/control state, runs the bounded drive-control state-9 wrapper, and restarts coroutine 1 at the initialization, status, drive-state, or startup-sequence entry according to the observed result flags.

Accepted C reconstruction: src/startup/startup_status_coroutine1.c (behavior-tested). Scheduler-installed no-input coroutine-one entry; every reachable route is non-returning, with native ERET retained as unreachable fallback. Preserves initial reset/D6/P1 actions, persistent and retained-media status normalization, pending-status mapping, status-four P3/configuration flag sequence, and each status-specific cooperative or tight indicator loop. Setjmp-backed host tests cover every terminal loop class; Keil C251 5.60 OPTIMIZE(0)/(8) verifies direct P1/P3 bits, helper calls and ERET; reduced A251 passes after same-address assembly removal.

Accepted C reconstruction: src/startup/startup_media_state_initialization.c (behavior-tested). No explicit inputs/result; native near RET. Preserves the sixteen-word, six-byte and 160-word bounded clears, ordered direct-bit and volatile mask resets, fixed radial/speed/timeout defaults, retained-configuration branch, seven subordinate helper calls and optional indexed-state-four position capture. Focused host tests pass; Keil C251 5.60 OPTIMIZE(0)/(8) verifies direct bits, near ClearTemporaryWriteSpeedReductionState LCALL, helper call classes and RET; reduced A251 passes after same-address assembly removal.

Accepted C reconstruction: src/startup/indexed_read_state_configuration.c.

Firmware 1.04 RAM:f859f0..RAM:f85d73 is a no-input near-RET worker. It normalizes RAM:001132, selects the lead-in or TOC acquisition tuple, derives RAM:000ff7 from the applicable endpoint divided by 75, initializes operating-code/media-coroutine state, and dispatches exact RAM:00130a cases. High P-code confirms explicit cases 0,1-7,9,0x0a,0x0c,0x0e,0x11-0x17,0x1f,0xf2-0xf4,0xf6,0xf9,0xfd and 0xff. State 0x1f clears six interleaved RAM:00f9ab/00f9ac entries and sets BITS:0037; state 0xf9 writes P3.0/P3.1 directly. The final call loads WR6=1 before RAM:fd7b56, whose XRL WR4,WR4 clears only the upper seed word.

Focused host tests cover target/endpoint selection, every explicit state class, both state-0x1f media routes, speed/P3 changes and final override. Keil C251 5.60 optimization 0/8 emits direct bits, WR6 seed one, expected call classes and RET; ProcessDriveStateMachine emits LCALL. Keil A251 4.69 rebuilds after removal of the obsolete 900-byte body/export.

Non-returning coroutine-1 media-state loop. Dispatches MediaCoroutineState values zero, one, two, three, five, and six to their cooperative processing paths; unexpected states enter the terminal loop.

Algorithm:
Calls the controller-command capture finalizer, clears the source state bits, then sets RAM:001306 bit three.

Parameters:
No explicit value parameters.

Returns:
RET.

Evidence:
Firmware 1.04 canonical bytes at RAM:f85e15..f85e41; direct instruction review. Exact A251 boundary in src/platform/media_interrupt_leaves.a51.

Algorithm:
Clears source state bits, resets controller port state, conditionally copies RAM:000e4f to RAM:000e50, and writes zero to XDATA:806a.

Parameters:
No explicit value parameters.

Returns:
RET.

Evidence:
Firmware 1.04 canonical bytes at RAM:f85e42..f85eab; direct instruction review. Exact A251 boundary in src/platform/media_interrupt_leaves.a51.

Processes MediaCoroutineState zero. It initializes controller and media flags, cooperatively waits for the state-zero setup condition, selects requested operating code one or eight from the observed media mode, and updates the shared drive-control state. No arguments or scalar return value.

Attempts the state-zero to state-three transition. It requires an active indexed drive state with code 0x1f, nonzero acquisition state, zero RAM:00fab0, and state-1302 bit 2 clear; then it sets that bit, stores acquisition state one, and selects MediaCoroutineState three. No arguments or scalar return value.

Processes MediaCoroutineState one.

Algorithm:
- Normalizes acquisition flags and selects the operating code and signed target.
- Acquires and validates disc position, configures controller channels/shadows, and services captured Q packets.
- Routes active/inactive indexed states, state-five calibration, cooperative yields, restarts, retries, and completion.

Parameters:
- None.

Returns:
- No scalar value; native near RET after terminal handled/completed states.

Reconstruction: accepted in src/startup/media_coroutine_state1.c. Focused route tests pass. Keil C251 5.60 OPTIMIZE(0/8) confirms direct P3 bits, canonical mixed LCALL/ECALL classes and RET; the sole caller emits LCALL. Keil A251 rebuilds after removal of the same-address 1,045-byte body/export.

Algorithm: requires RAM:00f79b bit zero and either the enabled/collected Q packet kind-two pair or an enabled kind-three-or-four option with collected kind three. On success, clears RAM:000fbc, updates RAM:000fba, sets P3.0, clears P3.1, sets media coroutine state three, and returns two; otherwise returns zero.

Parameters: none.

Returns: ACC status 0 or 2; RET.

MediaCoroutineState two acquisition/recovery worker.

Algorithm:
Adjusts target and operating-code state, acquires disc position, optionally applies dynamic port-80A8/A9 tolerance, configures the normal or alternate controller path, captures Q or three-byte packets while servicing eight-channel and command-0E measurements, and retries failed capture/calibration with speed reduction.

Confirmed from every instruction in firmware 1.04 RAM:f86475..RAM:f86894. R12 is a function-owned controller-gate bypass: set when RAM:000e46 == 1, or when RAM:000ff9 bit 2 is clear, RAM:00f9e9 bit 2 is set, and BITS:001c/001d are both clear. R13 is consecutive pulse successes, signed R14 is the retry count initialized/reset to 3, and R15 is the 25/70 pulse threshold. The post-acquisition wait is gated by BITS:0013 and repeatedly tests signed RAM:001034; it is not a RAM:000f46 test.

Parameters:
None.

Returns:
No portable scalar result; native near RET. Results are published through shared RAM and controller state.

Reconstruction:
Accepted C implementation is src/media/read_acquisition_state.c. Focused host control-flow tests pass; C251 5.60 O0/O8 builds with zero diagnostics and direct BITS accesses; the sole caller uses LCALL; the obsolete same-address 1,056-byte A251 literal body/export is removed.

Refreshes the target-derived radial value, computes the absolute difference between ReadAcquisitionTarget and CurrentDecodedFramePosition divided by 3000, and returns a frame tolerance in WR6. Speed 0x20 or above selects 250, speed 0x18 selects 180, and lower speeds clamp the quotient to 15..120.
Calls ConfigureControllerPorts8079And809DAnd809F only when bit 6 of RAM:00fae0 is clear. No arguments or scalar return value; the physical meaning of that mode bit remains unassigned.
Writes controller port 0x8079 as 0x14 or 0x94 according to RAM:001008 state two, then writes 0x40 to port 0x809d and 0xb0 to port 0x809f.

Processes MediaCoroutineState three. It restores the retained acquisition target, configures the controller operating state, selects the requested operating code, and handles exact zero, minus-one, and one acquisition results before continuing indexed-state or track-target processing. No arguments or scalar return value.

Services the controller/Q-capture auxiliaries used by MediaCoroutineState three. It conditionally invokes the shared media Q-packet service, clears ReadAcquisitionControlFlags bit 6 through the conditional operating-disable path, and starts the state-three capture/reinitialization attempt when BITS:000e is set. No arguments or scalar return value.

Attempts the MediaCoroutineState-three Q-capture and controller reinitialization path. It rearms packet capture with a bounded countdown, cooperatively processes packets and pulse checks, and on the accepted packet condition resets drive-control state, runs controller calibration, and selects state seven. No arguments or scalar return value.

Services indexed-drive transitions for media coroutine state three. It dispatches state 0x0c, applies the signed state-0x0e countdown restart test, advances state 0x13, routes state 0x1f and state six services, and manages the state-four/state-nine speed, countdown, flag, coroutine-installation and restart transitions. No arguments; returns normalized false in ACC through near RET. Accepted maintainable C: src/media/state3_indexed_transitions.c. Focused host tests cover all state classes and threshold/transition boundaries; Keil C251 5.60 optimization-zero/eight and reduced A251 4.69 pass. The obsolete same-address 590-byte assembly body/export was removed.

Processes media coroutine state five. Initializes control/controller state, runs bounded read-position acquisition with status-two target restoration, applies controller/target setup, polls three-byte packets, tracks decoded position, services indexed state, and preserves distinct external-completion, controller-error and indexed-completion cleanup orders. No arguments or scalar result; native near RET. Saved DR12 and the nine-byte local frame are entirely function-owned. Accepted maintainable C: src/media/coroutine_state5.c. Focused retry, packet, completion, error and loop tests pass; Keil C251 5.60 optimization-zero/eight confirms direct BITS:0033 access and canonical call classes, and reduced A251 4.69 passes after the obsolete 605-byte body/export was removed.
Initializes media-state-five control state: defaults threshold/flags, clears BITS:0036, and requests RAM:00fb69 bit zero when BITS:0031 or indexed state four is active.

Initializes the media-state-five controller path. It initializes position/controller state, runs two subordinate setup helpers, derives whether write-speed reduction is allowed from RAM:00fad7 bits 0, 1, and 12 plus RAM:001008, enables controller operation, issues controller command 06 selector 0x10 and stores its result in RAM:000fcd, recomputes the state-five controller threshold, and propagates RAM:00f971 bit zero into ReadAcquisitionControlFlags bit five. No arguments or scalar return.

Consumes a signed position-window value in DR4 and returns status 0, 1, or 2 in ACC through near RET. Applies the window to ReadAcquisitionTarget; handles acquisition result 0/1/0xff, tolerance retry, operating-profile transitions, scaled position waits, direct P0.7 recovery, readiness probes, and conditional target restoration. Maintainable C accepted in src/media/state5_read_acquisition_sequence.c: focused route tests pass; Keil C251 5.60 optimization 0/8 confirms direct P0.7 access, native call classes, and RET; the sole reconstructed caller emits LCALL; Keil A251 4.69 rebuilds after removal of the obsolete same-address 1,210-byte body/export.
Consumes a signed acquisition target in DR4 and selects controller parameters from that target, the current and secondary operating codes, and retained parameter words.

Services media-state-five controller and operating updates. It advances operating-update stages for media type two and controller-state bits 1..2 set, services position/controller helpers, converts RAM:000fd0 bit three into four SFR-bit requests, samples controller thresholds when enabled, refreshes the media-type-one controller profile when the secondary operating code is 0xff and the position coordinate changed, or invokes the media-type-two update helper. No arguments or scalar return.

Computes the signed media-state-five position window.

Algorithm:
- Snapshots the requested speed and conditionally caps the effective speed at 16.
- Computes the absolute signed target/current separation in 75-frame units.
- Applies the exact speed, media-type, negative-target and distance-bucket multipliers.
- Adds speed-specific offsets and applies the target-dependent 0x816 terminal clamp.

Parameters:
- None; entry ACC is dead scratch.

Returns:
- Signed 32-bit frame window in DR4 through native near RET.

Reconstruction: accepted in src/media/state5_position_window.c. Focused boundary tests pass. Keil C251 5.60 OPTIMIZE(0/8) confirms arithmetic ECALLs, DR4 result and RET. Keil A251 rebuilds after removal of the same-address 624-byte body/export.
When the active indexed-state code is 0xf6, stores countdown 20 at RAM:001202 and applies the scaled EA/EB controller-parameter writer with zero in WR6. No arguments or scalar return value.
Consumes a signed target in DR4 and gates the downstream controller action on CurrentDecodedFramePosition exceeding target + 225 frames together with the observed state flags.

Algorithm: compares prior/current decoded frame positions, marking RAM:00f978 bit one on a signed discontinuity of at least 750 frames unless bit zero suppresses it. With position tracking enabled and packet class two, uses the last TOC track tuple (or default endpoint) plus 9,000 + 20 frames to detect the terminal window and clears/sets the associated outcome bytes.

Parameters: prior frame position in native DR4.

Returns: current decoded frame position in DR4; RET.

Algorithm:
Consumes the secondary operating-code update trigger. When RAM:000fd0 bit 3 is set, clears it and sets BITS:003b, BITS:0039, BITS:003a, and BITS:0036 before invoking the secondary operating-code worker.

Parameters:
No explicit value parameters.

Returns:
RET.

Evidence:
Firmware 1.04 canonical bytes at RAM:f87a7c..f87a9f; direct branch and LCALL review. Exact A251 boundary in src/platform/media_interrupt_leaves.a51.

If controller port 0x8011 bit 1 is set and the current operating code is one of 0x14, 0x18, 0x20, 0x28, or 0x34, copies that code to SecondaryOperatingCode. Code 0x14 additionally requires the secondary code to hold sentinel 0xff. No arguments or scalar return value.

Processes media coroutine state six as an ordinary near-return worker. No explicit inputs or scalar result; the original saved R15 is function-owned. It clears BITS:0039, evaluates the speed-reduction predicate, dispatches media type two to its measurement retry, temporarily replaces and restores RAM:000e43 while selecting P3 direction, chooses RAM:000fe9 from lead-in, summed lead-out plus 0xa82, or fixed 0x34bc0, runs the state-six calibration sequence, and handles success reacquisition or failure cleanup. Statuses 2/3/4 remain protected. YieldCoroutine1 returns to this body; there is no stack-context transfer. Accepted C: src/platform/media_coroutine_state6.c; focused host tests plus C251 optimization-zero/eight and reduced A251 pass; same-address assembly body removed.

Acquires the current disc read position with at most three attempts, reinitializing the controller operating state between eligible failures. It restores the 150-frame target when needed, maps controller-reinitialization failure to read result seven, and publishes the exact media coroutine failure states before yielding. No arguments; returns Boolean success in ACC and terminates with ERET.

Executes the complete media-state-six controller calibration sequence. No explicit inputs; ACC returns the unsigned sequence status through RET, and saved DR12 is function-owned. The worker performs initial and near-target positioning under signed countdowns, clears sixteen sample words before each mode-two read-path attempt, evaluates the E2/profile position window, stabilizes four mode-three sample attempts, copies successful RAM:00facf calibration to RAM:001589 and RAM:00ef85, optionally runs ten mode-four terminal attempts, sets BITS:0039, and routes nonzero terminal states through EvaluateMediaState6CalibrationResultAndRetry. Accepted C: src/platform/media_state6_controller_calibration_sequence.c; focused host tests plus C251 optimization-zero/eight and reduced A251 pass; same-address assembly body removed.

Positions the read-acquisition path for one media-state-six calibration target mode. Unsigned target_mode enters in ACC; Boolean require_tolerance enters in R7; normalized Boolean status returns in ACC through RET. Modes zero through four retain distinct target and operating-code formulas. Failed acquisition permits at most three controller reinitializations; result 0xff repeats only for media state six with RAM:000e3f equal to one. Optional tolerance accepts exact result one and clears its restart bit after the first rejection. Mode two with RAM:000ff5 bit twelve set initializes signed RAM:001217 to 100 and reacquires until expiry. Accepted C: src/platform/controller_state6_calibration_positioning.c; focused host tests plus C251 optimization-zero/eight and reduced A251 pass; same-address assembly body removed.

Accepted C reconstruction: ReturnMediaState6CalibrationSuccess (src/platform/status_mapping.c).
Native ABI: Original returns ACC=1 with no other state change.
Behavior: None.
Validation: full instruction and return test review
Tests: reconstruction_foundation_tests Release result vector

Accepted C reconstruction: ReturnMediaState6CalibrationSequenceSuccess (src/platform/leaf_workers.c).
Native ABI: No input; ACC returns the fixed byte one. Internal reconstruction uses C ABI.
Behavior: None.
Validation: full two-instruction review and caller review
Tests: reconstruction_foundation_tests fixed ACC return value

Behavior reconstructed in C (src/platform/leaf_workers.c). Caller must enter with RAM:001203 positive: the native stack-local terminal-status byte is otherwise uninitialized. Arms controller packet capture, parses until a non-0xfe result, and applies signed target through target+4 and target+6 windows. Valid pulse-window packets advance RAM:000fef/000fee; terminal fee > 100 sets target 150, media state three, and status 0x1d. Other terminal paths return 0 or 2 after clearing RAM:001301 bit zero.

Runs the controller read-path calibration sequence at signed targetFramePosition from DR4. It applies the current operating profile, waits past three target offsets derived from the operating code, probes read-path readiness and its final operating window, and restores the read path on the terminal failure. Returns status zero on success or two on failure in ACC; terminates with RET.

Accepted C reconstruction: FUN_RAM_f8873d (src/platform/leaf_workers.c).
Native ABI: No scalar arguments or result; native RET exit. Calls the coroutine-one yield boundary.
Behavior: For indexed state 0x0a, temporarily publishes the low byte of RAM:0011f0 divided by 0x0e10 to RAM:001009, starts the P3 pattern, yields until RAM:000e3f is one, then restores RAM:001009.
Validation: Full instruction, caller, nonzero-divisor, state gate, P3-pattern, coroutine-yield loop, and restored-status review.
Tests: reconstruction_foundation_tests inactive gate, quotient publication/restoration, immediate completion, and two-yield completion

Algorithm:
Selects the direction-dependent read-acquisition target. On success it conditionally prepares controller ports and moves the pickup in ten-unit chunks.

Parameters:
No explicit value parameters.

Returns:
RET with the target-selection result in ACC.

Evidence:
Firmware 1.04 canonical bytes at RAM:f8877b..f887d3; direct control-flow review. Exact A251 boundary in src/platform/media_interrupt_leaves.a51.

Behavior reconstructed in C (src/platform/leaf_workers.c). Valid ACC input statuses 0, 1, and -1 respectively complete/restart read-position acquisition, service operating/Q capture or yield, and clear the retry marker. Statuses other than 0, 1, and -1 enter the canonical terminal self-loop at RAM:f88902; the C-facing model deliberately never maps them to an ordinary return. The fixed native controller-disable, Q-capture, and coroutine-restart calls use narrow adapters; P3.0 set/P3.1 clear stays atomic.

Behavior reconstructed in C (src/platform/leaf_workers.c). Decrements signed RAM:001007. A negative result restores the fallback state from RAM:00f79a; otherwise it resets drive control and invokes the state-one calibration worker through narrow fixed-input adapters. Calibration failure either reloads three attempts for RAM:001308=1/RAM:00fbf1=0 or publishes the exact status-seven fallback. P3.0 set/P3.1 clear remains atomic.

Behavior reconstructed in C (src/platform/leaf_workers.c). When RAM:001008 is one and signed RAM:001235 exceeds 0x00020f57, initializes the calibration byte, sets RAM:001306 bit six, persists the calibration block, writes RAM:00fab0, atomically sets P3.0/P3.1, and invokes stages four then five through narrow native adapters. ACC returns Boolean.

Behavior reconstructed in C (src/platform/leaf_workers.c). Returns ACC false unless RAM:001008 is one and signed RAM:001235 exceeds 0x0000b2b5; then invokes the RAM:f8e41c port-8097 calibration worker through a narrow native adapter and returns true.

Behavior reconstructed in C (src/platform/leaf_workers.c). Retains signed position comparisons against RAM:000e3b, 37/75/112-frame boundaries, timer RAM:000fd1, and signed four-observation counter RAM:000fd2. ACC returns Boolean.

Behavior reconstructed in C (src/platform/leaf_workers.c). ACC selects a signed three- or 300-frame tolerance; the function dispatches RAM:000fbe modes 0..5, retains exact RAM:00f2b9/ RAM:2bb042/ RAM:2bb03e track-MS F table formulas, and returns action 0/1/2 in ACC. Direction terminology remains a neutral software-bit label.

Behavior reconstructed in C (src/platform/leaf_workers.c). ACC selects a signed three- or 300-frame tolerance. The worker dispatches modes 0..5, using parsed-Q bit three, exact TOC/PMA tuples, and the staged target bound; ACC returns action 0, 1, or 2. Direction terminology remains a neutral software-bit label.
Copies DecodedQTrackNumber to both read-acquisition track selectors and CurrentDecodedFramePosition to ReadAcquisitionTarget.

Behavior reconstructed in C (src/platform/leaf_workers.c). Uses narrow native bit-space readers for BITS:0013/001b/001c/001d and retains every signed target adjustment, operating-enable call, and override order.

Services shared media Q-packet capture with a retry budget derived from CurrentOperatingCode. It rearms capture, tests the P1/CEX0 pulse threshold, processes captured packets, updates media flags, and cooperatively yields. No arguments or scalar return value.

For the observed active-media/configuration condition, disables controller operating state and waits on RAM:001215 after loading 20 or 40. It always clears ReadAcquisitionControlFlags bit 6. No arguments or scalar return value.
Returns Boolean true in ACC only when BITS:0032 is clear, MediaStateCountdownReload is nonzero, and signed MediaStateCountdown is negative. No input arguments.

Prepares the controller read-path parameters, selects one of the two readiness probes, retries at most three times with configuration restoration between attempts, and returns Boolean readiness in ACC. No arguments.

Runs a three-step controller read-path probe around the current decoded frame position, varies the controller port command, and waits for RAM:0180c0 bit 3. Returns Boolean completion in ACC. No arguments.
Toggles the controller-port handshake shadow around a byte read from RAM:0180c0 and returns Boolean bit 3 in ACC. No arguments.

Clears RAM:001302 bit 5, configures the adjacent controller read path, and cooperatively waits for that bit with the signed countdown at RAM:001217. Returns one in ACC after the completion delay and zero after timeout cleanup.

Restores the controller read-path ports and parameter D6. Boolean refreshDerivedParameters in ACC selects whether the current operating-code parameters and associated port state are refreshed. No return value.

Accepted C reconstruction: CopyCurrentDecodedFramePositionToReadAcquisitionTarget (src/platform/status_mapping.c).
Native ABI: No parameters or scalar return; source copies the canonical DR4 big-endian value through explicit byte reads and writes.
Behavior: Copies RAM:001235..001238 to RAM:000e3b..000e3e in ascending byte order.
Validation: full instruction and host trace review
Tests: reconstruction_foundation_tests Release exact four-byte copy trace

Returns in signed DR4 the integer conversion of 2000.0f * (ln((float)unsigned_WR6 / 32767.0f) / 2.3025851249694824f). This is exactly 2000 times the base-ten logarithm of the unsigned word normalized by 32767.

Binary32 natural logarithm approximation.

Algorithm:
Normalizes the positive input around sqrt(2), evaluates a four-stage continued fraction for ln(1+y), and adds the selected binary exponent multiplied by the binary32 ln(2) constant. Complete firmware 1.04 instruction review covers RAM:f8f38b..RAM:f8f479.

The native binary64 divide/decompose/scale prologue places its 1.41421356 threshold between adjacent binary32 mantissas 0x3504f3 and 0x3504f4. The accepted C implementation selects that boundary directly, then retains binary32 rounding after every continued-fraction operation.

Parameters:
DR4 / float value: IEEE-754 binary32 input.

Returns:
DR4 / float through native near RET: approximated natural logarithm.

Services one phase of the controller operating-threshold sample cycle after its countdown expires. It advances the two-bit phase field in RAM:000fd0, selects controller commands 0x16 and 0x06, samples port 0x80c7, applies exact operating-code and radial-position thresholds, updates consecutive-limit counters and latched maxima, and rearms the ten-tick countdown under interrupt exclusion. Probes controller parameters 0x14 and 0x16 through ports 0x80c4/0x80c5/0x80c7 using the exact state-dependent 0x50, 0x68, and 0x50 thresholds. On an eligible over-threshold result it extends the write-speed flags and invokes the temporary write-speed reduction policy. No arguments; returns Boolean continue status in ACC and terminates with ERET.
Updates the observed RAM:000fd0 mode bits, then writes zero to controller ports 0x80c4 and 0x80c5.

Accumulates one write-speed selection bit in the shared RAM:00fad7 flag word from CurrentDecodedFramePosition and CurrentOperatingCode. Codes below 0x14 are ignored. The signed position is partitioned by OperatingCodeThreshold1 through OperatingCodeThreshold3; the selected code band sets exactly one of bits 5 through 9, corresponding to the existing 40x through 16x speed-selection field. Conditionally constrains DiscReadSpeedLimitX from the retained controller-calibration byte at RAM:00f9e8. The exact threshold tree caps the multiplier to 8, 24, 32, or 40 and marks the associated probe flag. No arguments or return value.

Non-returning primary raw-read coroutine-2 pipeline installed by read and acquisition paths. Initializes the raw-read queue, repeatedly runs ProcessPrimaryRawReadPipelineStep, then enters FinalizeRawReadPipelineAndIdleCoroutine2. RAM:f900c0 is a fallthrough continuation of this function, not a function entry.

Processes one iteration of the primary raw-read pipeline and returns Boolean status in ACC. It coordinates acquisition targets, queue capacity, controller events, error mapping, and advancement of ReadPipelineTargetAddress.

Updates the primary raw-read pipeline's operating-code selection state. No arguments or scalar return; terminates with RET.

Throttles a raw-read producer when free ring capacity falls below the active threshold of 16, 64, or 128 descriptors. No arguments or scalar return; terminates with RET.

Initializes the controller and firmware shadows for a raw-read position probe. No arguments or scalar return; terminates with RET.

Controller read-event helper. In negative+C2+format-4 mode the branch at RAM:f9130d skips normal main-cursor reads, so MainDataRingCursor receives the auxiliary/C2 cursor retained on the stack. This explains an all-zero transfer when that ring contains zeros.

Processes the parsed-Q raw-read producer position when neither the payload-signature path nor its alternate producer mode is active. No arguments or scalar return; terminates with RET.

Processes decoded controller position for the primary raw-read producer. No arguments or scalar return; terminates with RET.

Processes one completed controller-read sector after the event handler has advanced its controller cursors. It decodes and validates the current position fields, classifies completion and raw-sector status, builds and enqueues the corresponding raw-read descriptor, advances ReadPipelineTargetAddress, and updates queue, countdown, recovery, and speed state. No arguments or scalar return; terminates with RET.

Builds or queues the phase-one raw-sector descriptor after a controller read-sector completion. It maps the observed read flags to exact descriptor statuses 0x1803/0x1804 or countdown statuses 0x1105/0x1106, invokes the shared countdown service where required, and returns false only when processing must stop. No arguments; returns Boolean continuation status in ACC; terminates with RET.

Handles raw-read descriptor production for the current completion flags. Depending on the active raw-read mode and status bits, it either builds the exact scratch descriptor directly or submits status 0x1105/0x1106 through the countdown-and-enqueue helper. No arguments; returns Boolean direct-build success in ACC and zero after queued handling; terminates with RET.

Builds an immediate scratch descriptor or services the queued raw-sector descriptor path for controller-read phase two. It selects exact base statuses 0x0000, 0x1105, 0x1106, 0x1803, or 0x1804 from the current read flags; one branch snapshots controller ports 0x8004..0x8007 and accepts an all-zero tuple. No arguments; returns Boolean ACC, true when the caller should take its immediate-completion path, and terminates with RET.

Services the parsed-Q raw-read descriptor countdown. Unsigned baseDescriptorStatus enters in WR6. When the countdown expires it either builds status 0x2100/mode-five scratch state after the P1.3 stability test, or derives the scratch descriptor from ParsedQStatusFlags and the supplied base status; it then enqueues the descriptor, advances ReadPipelineTargetAddress when required, and updates the acquisition-speed phase bytes. No scalar return.

Services the general raw-read descriptor countdown. Unsigned rawSectorSourceKind enters in ACC and unsigned baseDescriptorStatus in WR6; both are preserved until the countdown expires and are passed to BuildRawSectorDescriptorScratch. The routine maintains the special source-kind-three/status-0x1105 phase flag, enqueues the descriptor, advances ReadPipelineTargetAddress when required, and updates the acquisition-speed phase bytes. No scalar return.

Builds RawSectorDescriptorScratch from parsed Q status and baseDescriptorStatus in WR6. ParsedQStatusFlags bit two selects descriptor status 0x6300 with mode five. Otherwise, bit five clear sets RAM:000f2f bit six and selects status 0x6400 with mode five; bit five set selects baseDescriptorStatus | 0x0200 with mode three. The helper also forces RAM:000f2e to five and does not enqueue the descriptor.

Initializes the controller cursor-register handshake, clears the raw descriptor queue counters, derives its mask and high-water count from RawReadRingSlotCount, restores controller descriptor-table address 0x88bb, and clears associated transfer state and flags.
Non-returning coroutine-2 finalizer shared by the raw-read pipelines. Restores acquisition/read-speed state, requests the final acquisition transition when necessary, then yields coroutine 2 forever.

Consumes baseDescriptorStatus in WR6 and descriptorMode in ACC. After lazy controller-cursor initialization, either defers the descriptor while applying the exact raw-read timing/speed gates, or builds and enqueues the 22-byte raw sector descriptor. The enqueue path signals the consumer or advances ReadPipelineTargetAddress by one and resets the adjacent phase counters. No return value.

Lazily initializes controller buffer cursor registers 0x8004, 0x8005, and 0x8019 according to internal initialization bits. It also clears the associated shadows and controller status flags; it does not reset the software descriptor queue.
Non-returning alternate raw-read coroutine-2 pipeline. Initializes its queue and alternate-mode state, repeatedly runs ProcessAlternateRawReadPipelineStep, then enters the shared finalizer/idle sink.

Processes one iteration of the alternate raw-read pipeline and returns Boolean status in ACC. It requests the current or special acquisition target, waits on controller states five and six, and maps a terminal result.

No arguments or return value. Tracks raw-read producer position and arms capture at the prepared target. It aborts invalid/out-of-window acquisition or arms the raw-sector buffer at the target; special raw-read mode arms capture immediately. No arguments or scalar return; terminates with RET.
Advances staged ADR-1 Q positions by one frame. Absolute MSF always increments; RAM:0015a6 selects relative MSF decrement or increment. Packed-BCD frame wrap is 74 and second wrap is 59.

Resets the controller event-bit-7 transfer state, acknowledges the controller event, copies the active ten-byte metadata record into RAM:00faf2, and conditionally restarts the raw-read pipeline for command-state value seven.

Receives signed framePosition in DR4. Algorithm:
Invokes RAM:f9dec5 and returns through the native profile-selector calling frame.

Parameters:
Inherited native register frame.

Returns:
RET.

Evidence:

Programs the selected controller register profile under interrupt masking.

Parameters:
- profileSelector (ACC): unsigned fixed/generated profile selector.
- inherited R9: auxiliary-record index only when profileSelector is below 0x14; the generated route replaces it with profileSelector - 0x14.

Algorithm:
1. Clear BITS:0547, set RAM:000fca bit three, and publish it to RAM:018002.
2. Select RAM:f8363d + RAM:00f05f * 24 for selectors below 0x14, otherwise RAM:00e806 + (selector - 0x14) * 34.
3. Program 24 MMIO bytes; map encoded offsets 6, 9, 13, 16, 20, and 23 around the controller-register gap.
4. Copy four auxiliary bytes from the RAM:00e823 34-byte-record family.
5. Freshly read RAM:000fca, clear bits three/four, republish it, then set BITS:0547, BITS:0546, and SFR:A9.2.

Returns:
No scalar result; native RET.

Splits IEEE-754 binary64 input into integral and fractional parts by converting through the compiler's signed 32-bit integer helper. The integral binary64 value is written through the stack-supplied output pointer and the fractional part is returned in DR0:DR4; leave this composite ABI unforced.

Acquires the companion forty-frame type-two controller-record window beginning at ControllerRecordWindowBaseFramePosition. The whole sequence is retried at most three times. It takes no arguments and returns Boolean success in ACC.

Acquires a forty-frame type-two controller-record window beginning at ControllerRecordWindowMiddleFramePosition. It initializes raw-read type code ten, constructs relative and absolute Q MSF tuples, submits controller-buffer command 0x80, and emits descriptors in exact 5 + 32 + 2 + 1 frame groups while advancing the Q packet and ring position after every frame. The full sequence is retried at most three times. It takes no arguments and returns Boolean success in ACC.

Prepares the eight primary type-two controller-record slots. Boolean ACC selects whether each candidate begins from the current five-byte slot position or ControllerRecordGeometryTable0. Each candidate is transformed by (position + 150) / 32 * 39 before the indexed acquisition attempt. A rejected attempt marks the slot state one and shifts both the slot and source position backward by 32. Returns false only when the adjusted candidate crosses the signed RAM:00114f bound or a subordinate operation fails; otherwise returns true in ACC.

Acquires and constructs one primary Type-2 controller-record slot from signed startFramePosition supplied in DR0. Boolean acquisitionMode enters in ACC and unsigned recordSlotIndex in R7. It initializes the raw-read geometry, collects the fixed controller-record sequence, dispatches the mode-specific record builders, retries once after resetting the pipeline, and returns success in ACC; terminates with ERET.

Prepares the eight secondary type-two controller-record slots from ControllerRecordGeometryTable1. Boolean ACC is forwarded to the indexed acquisition attempt. A rejected attempt marks the slot state one, shifts both the slot and source position backward by 32, and rejects the sequence if the transformed position falls below ControllerRecordGeometryTable1[7] minus 0x4e0. Returns Boolean completion in ACC.

Acquires and constructs one secondary Type-2 controller-record slot. Boolean acquisitionMode enters in ACC, unsigned recordSlotIndex in R7, and signed startFramePosition in DR0. It publishes that position as ReadPipelineTargetAddress, emits the fixed 5 + 32 + 2 + 1 frame sequence, dispatches the indexed record builders, advances the raw-read descriptor/ring state, and retries the complete operation once after resetting the pipeline. Returns Boolean success in ACC; terminates with ERET.

Coordinates acquisition of controller-record index runs for the ACC operation mode. Mode three adjusts the terminal index from the current table segment before invoking the zero-state run scanner; ACC reports overall completion success.

Initializes expected descriptor count to ten, invokes ExecuteRawReadQRecordSequence with firstRecordIndex one so table record zero is preserved, clears the active flag on exit, and returns Boolean success in ACC.

Acquires the Type-2 controller-record sequence beginning at AtipLeadInStartFramePosition. It initializes raw-read mode one, walks the lead-in record window through the derived controller-record boundary, enqueues each captured descriptor, and retries after resetting the pipeline. Returns Boolean success in ACC; no arguments; terminates with ERET.

Acquires the Type-2 controller-record sequence containing the fixed thirteen-byte TDI payload. It resumes the main-data ring, uses the controller address returned by ResumeMainDataRingCursorFromLatestDescriptor, emits five prefix frames, 138 TDI payload frames, two suffix frames, and one terminal frame, and services pending host commands during the payload loop. It retries the complete sequence at most three times and returns Boolean success in ACC. No arguments: the apparent live DR4 value is produced by the first callee; terminates with ERET.

Acquires the Type-2 lead-out controller-record sequence. It resumes the main-data ring, starts from the controller record at RAM:2ba58d, emits five prefix records, the fixed 0x1a57-record body, optional two-record suffix, and one terminal record while advancing packed-BCD Q MSF state and raw-read descriptors. It retries the complete sequence at most three times and returns Boolean success in ACC. No arguments: the apparent live DR4 value is produced by ResumeMainDataRingCursorFromLatestDescriptor; terminates with ERET.

Receives a low-24-bit controller-buffer address in DR4 and a command parameter in ACC. It programs address bytes at ports 0x8010..0x8012, writes the parameter to port 0x8029, loads the fixed 00/e0/c3 triplet at ports 0x801f..0x8021, arms event 0x40, submits controller command 0x80, waits for ControllerEvent40CompletionFlag, and then disarms the event and clears the triplet. The physical transfer mode selected by the parameter remains unresolved.

Scans indices zero through WR6 inclusive in the table addressed by ControllerRecordIndexStateTableAddress. Each maximal run of zero-valued entries is passed to the 39-frame range acquisition worker. ACC supplies its operation mode and receives the worker's abort indication.

Acquires the inclusive controller-record index range WR6..WR4. Each index maps to 39 consecutive frames beginning at index * 39 + 145; the worker emits a 5 + 32 + 2 frame pattern, services pending host work, resets the raw descriptor ring, and refreshes affected type-3 record blocks. ACC selects operation mode and returns true when the range is aborted by shared operation state.

Translates the inclusive WR6..WR4 controller-record index range through the firmware segment-boundary tables. Every table entry whose state is exactly three causes its containing 32-position controller-record block to be refreshed; shared record cursors are reset when any block changed.
Copies the stack-supplied count of four-byte units from the DR4 source to DR0 + 0x00100000. Both addresses advance by four per unit. The mixed register/stack ABI remains intentionally unforced.
Copies exactly six bytes from far address DR4 to far address DR0 as three ordered 16-bit units. No caller establishes supported overlap semantics.

Completes the cooperative read-acquisition handoff. Shared READ CD and READ CD MSF execution body. It validates the decoded sector-selection fields, initializes raw-read mode state, classifies signed start positions at -1000, -20000, and -30000 into the established acquisition flags, starts or continues ExecuteRawSectorReadRange, and maps terminal failures to the exact recorded sense/information paths. Classifies a READ CD frame range against the applicable first- and last-track bounds. Signed startFramePosition enters in DR4 and signed endFramePosition in DR0. It selects parsed-TOC or working-track bounds, retains the last checked start, and asks MatchReadCdFramePositionToTrackRange to classify the start and end adjustments. Returns exact track-coverage class one or two in ACC; terminates with ERET.

Matches a READ CD target against an inclusive track-number range. Signed targetFramePosition enters in DR4, first and last track numbers enter in ACC and R3, and the caller-selected frameBias enters in WR0. The routine derives per-track frame bounds from raw-Q or track-table records, updates the selected track/phase state, and returns Boolean acceptance in ACC; terminates with ERET.

Maps signed logicalBlockAddress in DR4 through the applicable 19-byte TrackInformationTable record. The default result is the address plus the 150-frame LBA bias. When the shared layout-enable bit is set and the selected track record has flag bit zero and a nonzero packet size, it adds seven controller frames for each completed packet relative to that track's decoded MSF origin, stores the added adjustment at RAM:000f0c, and sets BITS:000c. Invalid or inapplicable track state follows the original flag-clearing exits.

Maps signed logicalBlockAddress in DR4 through the negative 32-data/7-overhead layout. With the shared layout-enable bit clear it returns address + 150 and clears BITS:000c. Enabled addresses from zero through 149 return unchanged; other addresses set BITS:000c and add the firmware's exact signed quotient/remainder adjustment, storing that adjustment at RAM:000f0c. This name describes arithmetic geometry only; the on-disc record class remains unidentified.

Maps signed logicalBlockAddress in DR4 through an alternate controller-record layout. With the shared layout-enable bit clear it returns address + 150 and clears BITS:000c. Otherwise it sets BITS:000c, combines signed divisions by 0x1100 and 32 with the original multiplication sequence, stores the adjustment at RAM:000f0c, and returns address + adjustment + 150. The unusual DR8/ACC/B sequence is preserved rather than reduced to an unverified portable-C formula.

Selects a signed logical-to-controller-frame mapping for logicalBlockAddress in DR4. Runtime state at RAM:0015d7, a mode bit derived from RAM:000c88, address sign, and MaximumWriteLogicalBlockAddress choose the track-packet, negative 32+7, or alternate-record transform. BITS:001b is cleared on entry and set only for the negative 32+7 branch. The selected transform returns the mapped frame position in DR4.

Validates CommandStartLogicalBlockAddress and CommandTransferBlockCount under the alternate layout selected by RAM:0015d7. It applies the exact negative-address, current media-end, runtime-mode, and opcode-0xb9 exceptions. Rejected ranges publish sense 05/2100 or 05/6400 and an information value adjusted by RAM:000f0c; ACC returns false. Accepted ranges return true. The unnamed mode bits remain neutral.

Executes the range in CommandStartLogicalBlockAddress and CommandTransferBlockCount for ordinary VERIFY, WRITE AND VERIFY readback, and one internal media-state caller. It rejects FullTocSummaryFlags masked value one with exact sense 05/6400 and the command LBA as information, optionally maps the start through MapLogicalBlockAddressToControllerFramePosition, validates the range, resets the raw-read queue, starts coroutine 2 at the primary raw-read pipeline, and cooperatively polls PollReadVerifyRawDescriptorStatus while it returns 0xfe. Terminal status one publishes no sense; all exits restore the pipeline's idle coroutine and control bits.

Polls one step of the active read/verify raw-descriptor range. ACC returns 0xfe while pending, one when HostTransferCompletedBlockCount equals HostTransferTotalBlockCount, and zero on terminal failure. A queued acceptable descriptor increments the completed count and consumes one entry. Under the mapped-address mode it handles descriptor subtype 0x0a specially or resets the queue and restarts coroutine 2 at the mapped base-plus-progress position. A nonzero pending error code selects sense and information values from firmware tables before returning zero.

Performs the one-sector acquisition used by READ HEADER. It rejects FullTocSummaryFlags masked value one with sense 05/6400, validates the command start through ValidateCurrentCommandLogicalBlockRange, forces the internal block count to one, starts or repositions the primary raw-read pipeline, and cooperatively polls PollReadHeaderSectorAndTransferResponse while it returns 0xfe. All exits restore the pipeline's idle coroutine and control bits.

Polls the READ HEADER sector acquisition. It returns 0xfe in ACC while controller or descriptor data is pending, zero on failure, and one after constructing and transferring the response. The exact eight-byte response contains the raw descriptor's mode byte, three zero bytes, and either a zero-prefixed three-byte MSF tuple or a four-byte LBA selected by the CDB MSF bit. Transfer length is clamped to eight.

With DR4=start, DR0=end, and ACC=playback mode: equal positions set RAM:000c8c=3, store the target at RAM:000c8e, then call DispatchAndWaitForReadAcquisitionResult at RAM:fdcc22. Unequal positions set RAM:000c8d from ACC nonzero, store DR0-DR4 modulo 32 bits at RAM:000f36, clear BITS:0018, and call StartFormat2RawSectorReadAtFramePosition at RAM:fd4f13 using DR4.

Parameters:
DR4 signed start frame, DR0 signed end frame, ACC playback-mode Boolean; DR12 is saved/restored.

Returns:
ERET; no ordinary C return value.

Evidence: live instructions/P-code, direct-callee documentation, exact byte extraction, and assertion-enabled host matrix.

Starts the controller/raw-read setup used by audio commands and the configured coroutine path. Receives signed framePosition in DR4, resets the relevant controller ports and shared state, then invokes ExecuteRawSectorReadRange for the one-frame range [framePosition + 2, framePosition + 3) with internal format code two. It conditionally rebuilds and applies the port-0x8087/0x808b shadows after the call.
Non-returning coroutine-0 worker installed by the indexed-state raw-sector read setup. Passes the configured RAM:00fbf8 value to the raw-sector range executor and then yields coroutine 0 forever.

Firmware 1.04 retained write-buffer snapshot validator. Rejects clear RAM:001159; otherwise compares controller-buffer checksum bytes 0x28e0..0x28e1 with RAM:fd5d8c's additive sum over 0x28e0 bytes. A mismatch clears RAM:001159. ACC Boolean return; ERET. C model and focused vectors are in src/platform/status_mapping.c.
Clears the Boolean staged WRITE BUFFER snapshot-valid latch at RAM:001159.
Sets the Boolean staged WRITE BUFFER snapshot-valid latch at RAM:001159 after successful validation.
Returns the normalized RAM:001159 staged WRITE BUFFER snapshot-valid latch in Boolean ACC.

Copies byteCount bytes from the RAM source in DR4 to successive controller-buffer offsets beginning at DR0 through WriteControllerBufferWindowByteAtomic. byteCount is an unsigned 16-bit caller-stack argument. This mixed register/stack ABI is deliberately left unforced.

Copies byteCount bytes from successive controller-buffer offsets beginning at DR4 to the RAM destination in DR0 through ReadControllerBufferByteAtomic. byteCount is an unsigned 16-bit caller-stack argument. This mixed register/stack ABI is deliberately left unforced.

Builds the 0x28e2-byte READ BUFFER mode-1/buffer-ID-2 snapshot in reserved controller-buffer memory, including headers, selected state/configuration data, and a trailing checksum. Returns 0x28e2 in WR6; HandleReadBufferCommand consumes that caller-visible register result as the transfer clamp.
Validates a WRITE BUFFER snapshot of the expected DR4 length: requires 0x28e2 bytes, compares fixed headers, verifies the trailing checksum, and returns Boolean ACC.

Restores the state payload previously serialized by BuildReadBufferMode1Id2Snapshot from reserved controller-buffer storage. It copies the fixed header-state fields, track-indexed six-byte records, controller workspaces, and bounded ten-byte record tables back into their RAM destinations. No arguments or scalar return; terminates with ERET.

Firmware 1.04 controller-buffer checksum worker. Reads exactly 0x28e0 bytes from the controller buffer starting at DR4 offset (native RAM:feea1c reader), accumulating modulo 65536; returns the WR6 sum, ERET. C model and focused vectors are in src/platform/status_mapping.c.

Recalculates both checksums in DriveConfigurationBuffer. It sums bytes 0x00..0x5d into the big-endian word at 0x5e and bytes 0x00..0x7d into the big-endian word at 0x7e.

Stores failureCode from ACC in logical drive-configuration byte 0x72, recalculates the primary and extended checksums, then invokes ProgramAndVerifyDriveConfiguration with Boolean false. All ten caller sites are validation-failure exits and supply observed codes 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, or 10.

Reads and validates the 160-byte persistent drive configuration image, copies a caller-supplied byte range into it, recalculates the primary and extended checksums, programs and verifies the configuration, and checks the stored checksum words. Invokes the runtime configuration programmer at RAM:ff4500 with Boolean ACC. Zero verifies the 0x60-byte primary and 0x40-byte extended regions; nonzero verifies only the extended region. Success resets the raw-read queue and returns true.
Reads big-endian configuration word WR6. The input is a word index; twice that index selects the logical split at byte offset 0x60 between RAM:ffc000 and RAM:ffa000.

Sums persistent logical configuration bytes 0x00..0x5d, read one at a time through ReadDriveConfigurationBytes, and returns the unsigned 16-bit checksum in WR6.
Requires logical configuration bytes 0x00..0x5d to be erased, then calculates both configuration checksums and invokes the runtime programming/verification path through RAM:ff4500.

Updates a byte range in the persistent drive-configuration image and programs it. The destination offset enters in DR4, source address in DR0, and byte count in the caller stack slot. Validates one 18-byte CD-TEXT pack selected by unsigned packIndex in DR4. Only exact header 0x8f accumulates nonzero payload lengths plus one: offsets 12..15 for type one and 4..7 for type two. A nonzero sequence discontinuity clears BITS:001e. Returns normalized Boolean in ACC through RET.

Consumes a four-byte state address in DR4 and newValue in R3. It replaces byte zero, computes the bitwise three-input consensus of old byte zero, newValue, and byte one, then ORs consensus bits into byte two where newValue is one and into byte three where newValue is zero. No scalar return.

Splits the R3 input byte into low and high nibbles and maps both through the adjacent standard hexadecimal seven-segment table at RAM:fee607. Maps zero to zero and the one-hot byte values 1 through 0x80 to one-based indices 1 through 8. Any other byte returns 0xff. Input enters in R3 and the result returns in R7.

Writes byteValue R3 to destinationAddress DR20, advances the far destination by one, and decrements 32-bit byteCount DR16 until zero. The do-while entry requires caller-established nonzero count. No scalar return.

For each unsigned WR18 window, reads a word from far DR20 and writes it to far DR24, then advances both addresses by one byte. The overlapping word-window behavior is preserved exactly; it must not be generalized to memcpy without caller preconditions.
Compares signed R3 with zero and toggles R3 bit seven only when the comparison reports negative. Returns the resulting byte in R3.
Compares signed WR2 with zero and toggles its low-byte R3 bit seven only when the comparison reports negative. Returns R3.
Compares signed DR0 with zero and toggles its low-byte R3 bit seven only when the comparison reports negative. Returns R3.
Computes the unsigned integer square root of the 32-bit value in DR4 using a 16-round restoring bit-pair algorithm and returns the floor result in DR4.

Clears R0 through R2 while retaining the inherited R3 byte, so DR0 equals the unsigned byte before displacement -0x1877; the 24-bit destination is RAM:ffe789 + value and the same byte is stored there. Main-image initialization bridge. RAM:ff2000 is a hardware/register initialization service, not a readable firmware-image window.
Disables the standard 8051 global interrupt-enable bit IE.EA and returns. It has no arguments or result.
Enables the three fixed main-firmware interrupt sources and returns.
Disables the two interrupt-control bytes and tail-jumps to InitializeAndEnterFirmwareMain. This function cannot return.
Zeros byteCount/2 consecutive 16-bit words beginning at the DR0 destination. All verified callers supply an even nonzero byte count in WR6.
Converts one packed-BCD byte in ACC to binary and returns the result in ACC: 10 * high_nibble + low_nibble.

Converts the three binary minute/second/frame bytes at DR0 to a signed frame position in DR4 using 60 seconds per minute and 75 frames per second. Under the established low-radial-position mode it conditionally adds 0x08ca according to RAM:00102f, RAM:00fb87 bit 5, and RAM:00114f.
ATA command 0xe6 sleep helper. Enables BITS:0547 (IE.EA), sets SFR:0087 PCON bit one (power-down), executes two NOPs, and returns through ERET after wake. No scalar input or result.

Resets raw-read option, format, progress, and status state; copies the decoded command block count and block size into the active host-transfer fields; and returns CommandStartLogicalBlockAddress plus 150 in DR4.
Decodes controller position bytes at RAM:018004..018006 as BCD. SpecialRawReadMode permits invalid/non-BCD fields and selected controller sentinel values that normal position synchronization rejects.

Returns Boolean readiness for the current media state. Media state zero succeeds immediately. Media state two fails immediately when the low nibble of RAM:001245 is zero. Other paths require architectural P1.3 at BITS:0483 to remain high for 19 consecutive samples within the bounded 38-sample wait. The physical meaning of P1.3 remains unresolved.
Atomically reads one byte from controller-buffer offset DR4 and returns it in ACC, preserving the interrupt-control SFRs.

Validates the current command's signed start LBA and unsigned block count. RAM:0015d7 selects the alternate validator. The ordinary path checks positive ranges against the greater of the two media-end positions and classifies accepted negative ranges into the firmware's -1000, -20000, and -30000 bands. Invalid ranges publish sense 05/2100, or 05/6400 for the special media-state rejection, with information equal to the command LBA minus RAM:000f0c. ACC is true only for an accepted range.
Sets the architectural IE.0/EX0 enable bit at BITS:0540 only when the shared pipeline-mode byte at RAM:00127e is nonzero. The physical source connected to external interrupt zero is not established.

Clears the architectural IE.0/EX0 enable bit at BITS:0540 only when the shared pipeline-mode byte at RAM:00127e is nonzero. The physical source connected to external interrupt zero is not established.

Byte-identical linked copy of RAM:fe02bd. Copies the unsigned 16-bit byte count at SPX-4 from DR0 to DR4 while incrementing only the low 16-bit pointer halves.
Converts three consecutive binary bytes beginning at the WR6 address to packed BCD in place.
Converts three consecutive packed-BCD bytes beginning at the WR6 address to binary in place.

Increments the three-byte packed-BCD MSF tuple at the WR6 address. Frames roll over at 75 and seconds at 60; minutes roll from 99 to 00 or A0 according to RAM:001033.

Summary
Firmware 1.04 binary64 exponent-scaling helper.

Algorithm
For nonzero input, adds the signed scale to the stored 11-bit exponent. Results below exponent one clear all bits. Results above 0x7ff first set the mantissa/exponent payload bits and then repack the wrapped signed exponent exactly as the canonical instructions do; this is deliberately not ordinary IEEE saturation. Zero bypasses unchanged.

Parameters
Maintainable C interface: binary64 value and signed 16-bit scale. The original private compiler-runtime mixed register/stack ABI is not asserted.

Returns
Scaled binary64 through native ERET.

Evidence
RAM:feee85..feef52 full 70-instruction review, raw-bit focused tests, C251/FLOAT64 O0/O8 listing verification, and reduced A251 rebuild.

Reconstruction
Accepted C: src/platform/float64_runtime_helpers.c. Former sole caller NaturalLogFloat32 is independently reconstructed; same-address assembly/DB body removed.

Summary
Firmware 1.04 binary64 mantissa/exponent decomposition helper.

Algorithm
Exact +0 writes exponent zero and returns unchanged. Every other raw payload writes stored exponent minus 0x3fe and replaces only the stored exponent field with 0x3fe, preserving sign and fraction. Subnormal payloads are deliberately not shifted; negative zero follows the nonzero raw-bit route.

Parameters
Maintainable C interface: binary64 value and signed 16-bit exponent output pointer. The original private compiler-runtime mixed register/stack ABI is not asserted.

Returns
Exponent-adjusted binary64 through native ERET and the signed exponent through the explicit pointer.

Evidence
